correctness.rationale: The forced-middle argument, edge-level strictness, and an independent-set bijection prove the complete weighted identity for every finite oriented simple graph and every positive three-level size. For connected bipartite graphs, exactly two orientations have no mixed vertex; all others give zero or are bounded by injection of 2^{|M|} independent-set copies into the underlying independent-set family, and the explicit double-star sequence approaches the sharp ratio 1/2. A binary-word recurrence gives 2F_n admissible path orientations. verify.py independently brute-forced 3473 finite instances/coefficient and recurrence checks, but the all-size proofs do not rely on finite exhaustion.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Published Datalog and homomorphism-duality results concern decision complexity and pp-constructibility. Work on acyclic orientations and linear extensions counts extensions of partial orders, not all maps into the fixed three-level template. A general #CSP enumeration algorithm could compute these counts but does not by itself state the explicit equality or sharp factor-1/2 orientation gap. Other three-layer targets are covered directly by the new weighted formula, so the target T3 case is not used to evade a stronger claim.

value.rationale: The canonical mixed-vertex neighbourhood determines an entire weighted solution-count polynomial for a natural finite-template CSP family; the stability theorem then gives both a rigidity characterization of maximizing orientations and the optimal universal factor-1/2 gap, exhibited by a motivated sequence of trees. This is a substantive exact-counting and extremal structural relation, not solely a reformulation of the known existence test.
